get.description: Returns the listener, including its default pool and operating status.

put.description:
Replaces the listener's target specification as a whole. The body carries the complete desired state of every field `publicCloud.loadbalancer.ListenerPutTargetSpec` exposes, so read the listener first and restate every value you want to keep: a field left out of `targetSpec` is cleared, not carried over from the stored specification.

This matters most for the collection-valued and security-relevant fields. Leaving `allowedCidrs` out clears the allow list and reopens the listener to every source. Leaving `sniContainerRefs` out removes every SNI certificate, and leaving `defaultTlsContainerRef` out removes the default certificate. Leaving `insertHeaders` out stops every header from being inserted, and leaving `tlsVersions` out clears the TLS version restriction. Each of these is replaced as a whole — there is no per-element merge.

The create-only fields `protocol` and `protocolPort` cannot be changed once the listener exists. They are deliberately absent from the update model, and sending one is rejected with a 400.

`name` is required.

The optional `checksum` guards against a lost update: when supplied it must match the listener's current checksum or the request is rejected with a 409 checksum mismatch. Omitting it skips the check and forces the write (last-write-wins).

targetSpec.name: my-listener-renamed

Update load balancer listener.summary: Rename the listener. The body is the complete target spec: every timeout, the default pool and the TLS fields are restated so that none of them is cleared

put.description:
Replaces the pool's target specification as a whole. The body carries the complete desired state of every field `publicCloud.loadbalancer.PoolUpdateTargetSpec` exposes — `algorithm`, `description`, `healthMonitor`, `name` and `persistence` — so read the pool first and restate every value you want to keep: a field left out of `targetSpec` is cleared, not carried over from the stored specification. Leaving `healthMonitor` out deletes the pool's health monitor, and leaving `persistence` out disables session persistence.

The create-only field `protocol` cannot be changed once the pool exists. It is deliberately absent from the update model, and sending it is rejected with a 400.

The monitor `type` is immutable once the monitor exists, so restate the current type.

The optional `checksum` guards against a lost update: when supplied it must match the pool's current checksum or the request is rejected with a 409 checksum mismatch. Omitting it skips the check and forces the write (last-write-wins).

get.summary: List the lakehouses of your project.
get.description:
Each lakehouse is an IAM resource of type `publicCloudProject/lakehouse`, a sub-resource of the project, with the URN `urn:v1:<eu|ca|us>:resource:publicCloudProject:<projectId>/lakehouse/<lakehouseId>`: an IAM policy can grant actions on one lakehouse and on everything under it. Where IAM authorizes the calls, the list holds only the lakehouses that your IAM policies let you read.

The list has no region filter: to keep the lakehouses of one region, select them on `targetSpec.region`.

post.summary: Create a lakehouse in your project.
post.description:
Creates the lakehouse asynchronously. The response is the lakehouse in CREATING, with the creation task in `currentTasks`: follow it on the task routes of the lakehouse, or read the lakehouse until its `resourceStatus` is READY or ERROR.

The lakehouse is created with its first catalog, described by `targetSpec.catalog`. Creates the role assignment asynchronously. The response is the role assignment in CREATING, with the creation task in `currentTasks`: follow it on the task routes of the role assignment, or read the role assignment until its `resourceStatus` is READY or ERROR.

The identity is a user, a service account or a group of the lakehouse, and `identity.type` must match it, or the creation is refused with a 400. A role assigned to a group applies to every member of the group. Without `scope`, the identity holds the role as it is defined; with a CATALOG scope, it holds the permissions of the role only within that catalog. The predefined roles LAKEHOUSE_ADMIN and USER_ADMIN cover the whole lakehouse and refuse a scope with a 400.

The same role cannot be assigned twice to the same identity with the same scope. The creation is refused with a 409 while the lakehouse, the role, the identity or the scope catalog is being deleted, or while the same role assignment is still being removed. A role assignment cannot be changed after creation: delete it and assign the role again.

Assigning a role gives data access: whoever may call this route can give any role of the lakehouse to any of its identities. Management rights, granted in OVHcloud IAM, are not affected.

put.summary: Update a user of your lakehouse.
put.description:
Replaces the user's target specification as a whole. The body carries the complete desired state of every field `publicCloud.lakehouse.UserUpdateTargetSpec` exposes — `description` — so read the user first and restate every value you want to keep: a field left out of `targetSpec` is cleared, not carried over from the stored specification.

The create-only fields `name` and `type` cannot be changed once the user exists. They are deliberately absent from the update model, and sending one is rejected with a 400.

On a READY user the change is applied at once: the response is 200 with the user READY. On a user in ERROR the change is applied asynchronously, even when the specification is unchanged, to bring the user out of ERROR: the response is 202 with the user UPDATING and the new task in `currentTasks`. The update is refused with a 409 while the user is CREATING, UPDATING or DELETING, and after a refused deletion, from which only a new deletion is accepted.

The optional `checksum` guards against a lost update: when supplied it must match the user's current checksum or the request is rejected with a 409 checksum mismatch. Omitting it skips the check and forces the write (last-write-wins).

The create-only fields `location`, `encryption` and `createFrom` cannot be changed once the volume exists. They are deliberately absent from the update model, and sending one is rejected with a 400.

post.description:
Creates a file storage, either empty or from a snapshot.

Without `createFrom`, `shareType`, `shareNetwork` and `size` are required.

With `createFrom.snapshotId`, the file storage is created from that snapshot, which must belong to the same project and be in the region set in `location.region`; an unknown snapshot is rejected with a 404. The snapshot must be available: a snapshot in any other status is rejected with a 409. `shareType` and `encryption` are the values of the snapshot's source file storage and are returned in `targetSpec`: requesting `encryption.enabled` true from a snapshot of an unencrypted file storage is rejected as an invalid parameter, and requesting `encryption.enabled` false from a snapshot of an encrypted file storage is ignored. `size` is optional: when omitted, the snapshot's size is used and returned in `targetSpec`, and a size smaller than the snapshot's size is rejected. `shareNetwork` is optional: when omitted, the share network of the snapshot's source file storage is used and returned in `targetSpec`, and a different share network is rejected.

`createFrom` is set at creation only and cannot be changed afterward.
